Succumb

suh-KUM · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To succumb is to give in or yield to a superior force, pressure, or overwhelming influence.

Despite months of chemotherapy, the family's beloved dog finally succumbed to the illness over the weekend.

Worked Example

After holding firm through weeks of negotiation, the small bookstore finally succumbed to the rising rent and closed its doors for good.

The bookstore didn't want to close -- it simply couldn't keep resisting the pressure any longer. That eventual giving-in to something stronger than yourself is exactly what succumb describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

yield: to give way under pressure or force

capitulate: to stop resisting and give in completely

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

resist: to withstand the force or effect of something

withstand: to remain undamaged or unaffected by something powerful

Where it sits · how complete the surrender is — waver → succumb → collapse

waver vs. succumb: To waver is simply to hesitate or become uncertain, well short of actually giving in.

collapse vs. succumb: To collapse is to give way completely and often suddenly, an even more total defeat than succumbing gradually.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — suc-

prefix — suc-: under (the form Latin sub- takes before a c)

root — cumb

root — cumb: to lie down (from Latin cumbere)

Put it together

Put it together: Succumb is built from suc- ('under' -- the form Latin sub- takes before a c) + cumb ('to lie down,' from Latin cumbere) -- literally 'to lie down under' something. It came to mean giving in to a force too strong to keep resisting.

Use the root in a new word: incumbent

Use the root in a new word: incumbent: The incumbent mayor was running for re-election against two new challengers.

Root Check

Word Choice

Succumb usually describes the losing side of a struggle -- illness, temptation, pressure, or an opposing force -- and is almost always followed by 'to,' as in 'succumb to the pressure.' It describes the losing side of a power struggle, the opposite of subjugate or usurp, which describe the side gaining control.
